correspondence.finding: The selected western opening and first four selected parts have no independently read source depiction in this pass.
No permitted source was read that depicts these selected parts or their shared joins.
The southeastward selected corridor has not been matched to a primary source map.
No primary map or route prose read in this pass identifies this selected lower approach.
The DFO planning publication lists Snowbank River among regional Arctic-char fishing locations, but its inspected description does not locate or depict this selected terminal.

The chosen eastern opening follows the unnamed westward feeder valley north of Sheep Mountain. The source depicts the feeder continuously westward into the labeled Wulik River. The selected line generalizes local bends and the junction approach; no intervening divide, lake or different drainage transfer is needed at ordinary corridor scale.

The feeder meets the north-to-south Wulik trunk. Repeated Wulik River labels follow the selected upper valley, including widened braided sections and intervening tributary entries. The stored parts remain within the same continuously depicted trunk corridor.

The selected Wulik corridor turns southwest past the Ferric Creek entry setting and continues to the clearly depicted West Fork Wulik River junction. The West Fork approaches separately from the north; the chosen line stays on the Wulik approach and the joined downstream braided trunk. Connected river linework covers every selected interval.

The braided Wulik continues southwest through the Ikalukrok Creek confluence setting and past the Tutak Creek entry, then bends toward the west. Ikalukrok is a separately labeled tributary corridor. Repeated Wulik labels and continuous channel linework identify the selected receiving river throughout these stored parts.

The lower Wulik remains continuously mapped through broad wetland surroundings, multiple branches and the southwestward delta approach. Nearby lakes and the separate Kivalina River corridor are distinguishable from the selected Wulik channel. Wetland symbols do not replace or interrupt the depicted through-channel.

The actual stored endpoint lies in the Wulik delta-channel and Kivalina Lagoon entry setting opposite the Kivalina settlement area. The source depicts the Wulik distributary connection into the lagoon. The short final generalized turn is interpreted within this terminal corridor; the selected path is not extended across the lagoon or through the coastal barrier to an open-sea mouth.

The inspected route comprises a mountain feeder, connected river valley, braided lower river and coastal delta. Adjacent lakes are not selected through-lake transfers. Kivalina Lagoon is the terminal receiving setting. No selected glacier, reservoir, canal or managed-diversion passage is depicted by the read source cartography.

The selected southern Canadian opening runs westward, turns north and then northeast toward the small southern arm of Whiting Lake. Both inspected federal views show this opening and much of the approach beyond the continuously depicted water network. The final approach also crosses the space between a separate southern stream and the lake arm without a mapped through-link. The earlier field and glacier prose describes the broader upper Whiting setting, but does not locate this entire selected path. Neither the chosen opening nor its full connection to the first depicted lake arm is established. This is a substantive source-correspondence gap, not a requirement for exact ice margins, banks or current flows.

From the first depicted southern lake arm, the selected route enters and traverses the elongated waterbody directly labeled Whiting Lake. The southern arm, central lake passage and north-end departure setting are visibly connected at ordinary lake scale. The lake name is retained as a component name, not assigned to the upstream opening or to the whole river group.

The outlet at the northern end of Whiting Lake continues through a braided valley, receives an eastern tributary, and bends northwest and west to join the larger Whiting corridor. The map directly labels this selected outlet reach South Whiting River. The entire remaining upper-stage fragment and its join with the next selected fragment are geographically accounted for. Kerr’s earlier field prose independently describes the South and North Whiting junction and the downstream border connection, without establishing a modern name-boundary vertex.

After the South Whiting junction, the selected lower-stage fragment follows the directly labeled Whiting River southwest and west across the international boundary. Connected channel polygons and braided reaches establish the selected upper portion of this fragment. Distinct South Whiting and Whiting reach names coexist; no single scalar name is extended across every component.

The selected route continues down the same broad braided Whiting valley, turns southwest below the Crescent Lake tributary, and follows the lower valley toward the coast. The overview and lower detail depict the channel throughout these parts. The independent Juneau State Land Plan map also labels the river and the separate Crescent Lake branch. The selected mainstem does not traverse Crescent Lake.

The last two selected parts lie in the connected lower Whiting braid and coastal-estuary approach. The stored endpoint is inside the mapped lower-river corridor, upstream of its wider opening into Port Snettisham; it is not extended to a different mouth point. The map and state planning source establish the local lower-river identity and coastal setting without requiring an exact modern shoreline or tidal boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and connected headward lake chain
correspondence.finding: The selected opening corresponds to the narrow blue-water lake/channel corridor immediately east of the railway, north of the separately drawn southwestern Broad River branch. The chosen opening is covered; it is not asserted to be the natural head of Broad River. The selected continuation follows the connected small-lake and blue-channel chain northeast of the opening. The original Herchmer hydrographic base depicts the connections; adjacent geological contacts and magnetic contours are not used as channels. The lakes have no directly read names. The selected route leaves the mapped headward lake chain and continues east across the Herchmer sheet edge into the overlapping provincial regional map. The regional map identifies the continuing feeder corridor as Hoot Creek. A separate southern branch belongs to the southwestern Broad River approach.

correspondence.component_scope: Hoot Creek and its Broad River junction
correspondence.finding: The eastward selected corridor corresponds to the connected Hoot Creek feeder in the provincial map, with the small side-water branches distinguished from the selected continuation. The selected eastward reach remains within the Hoot Creek corridor before its northward approach to the shared Broad River trunk. The map supplies the continuous through-link; proximity to a river label alone is not the evidence. The selected eastward feeder turns north and joins the Broad River corridor. The provincial original depicts Hoot Creek, the joining southern Broad branch and their continuing northward trunk. The park map overlaps the shared trunk, but does not supply the detailed headward lake chain.

The selected northward corridor follows the labelled Broad River on the overlapping provincial and park originals, west and north of the separately depicted Skidmore Lake. Side-water and lake outlines are not incorporated into the selected route merely because they are nearby. The selected change from the northward inland reach to the east-northeast middle course corresponds to the continuing Broad channel on both originals. The selected middle reach and the adjoining side-stream junctions correspond to the continuing Broad River corridor. The provincial original provides the more detailed tributary pattern; the park original independently depicts the shared named course.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower tributary joins and coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The selected lower approach follows Broad River through the western tributary-junction setting. The originals distinguish Kelsey Creek from the continuing Broad trunk; the provincial map also shows the Beale Creek network. These tributary names are not assigned to the whole selected system. The short selected north-northeast segment remains on the continuous lower Broad channel before the coastal turn, as depicted on the overlapping originals. The selected northeast continuation approaches the coastal bend on Broad River rather than following a neighboring coastal stream. The park original identifies the Broad management-camp area and adjacent coast.

The final selected eastward coastal bend corresponds to the distinct Broad River mouth entering Hudson Bay. The park original depicts its tidal-flat setting and distinguishes this outlet from the Owl River outlet farther south. The actual terminal is covered at ordinary corridor scale.
